topics.description: The foundation for first interactions: greeting people, saying goodbye, thanking, apologizing, asking someone to repeat information, describing language ability, and asking how to say an object’s name in Japanese.

lessons.objective: Use basic expressions to begin and end simple interactions and respond in common social situations, including when someone helps you.
lessons.aksaraNote: Hiragana introduction: recognize basic characters and read words. The practice also highlights character variations across printed and handwritten forms, long vowels, and the small っ used for doubled consonants.

activities.explanation: Choose a greeting that fits the time of day and the situation. This activity distinguishes morning, daytime, and evening greetings, and introduces both more polite and more casual forms.

grammar.grammarId: There is no formal Grammar Notes section in this lesson.

culturalNote.content: The etiquette of ojigi (bowing) when greeting or thanking someone; why sayoonara is not used for every type of goodbye; and the different contexts for using sumimasen and arigatoo.

kanjiWords: The specific writing-system materials in Lesson 1 are Hiragana Words and the Hiragana chart
